*UPDATED*
SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JUNE 6, 2022 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
COUNCILMEMBER JOHNSON WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM 13141 DROXFORD STREET, CERRITOS, CA 90703, AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE.
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY, JUNE
6, 2022, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. COUNCILMEMBER JOHNSON
PARTICIPATED VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM 13141 DROXFORD STREET, CERRITOS, CA
90703, AND THE AGENDA WAS POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE
CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor/Chair Vo.

3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Bruce Barrows
  Mayor/Chair Chuong Vo

4.  Public Comments

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

5.  New and Old Business

5A.  Review and consideration of the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Preliminary Combined Financial
  Program for the City of Cerritos and the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment
  Agency (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The City Attorney stated Councilmember Johnson would recuse herself from participation in
  any discussion, deliberation, or voting on budget items related to the City’s contract with
  the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department.

  A staff report was given by Jeff Thielke, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed. Ken Pun, Auditing Consultant, was present at the meeting to answer any
  questions from the City Council.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Include the financial adjustments and modifications recommended by staff for the
  Items summarized below (Items are detailed in the associated agenda report for this
  item) to the proposed Fiscal Year 2022-23 budget resolution, including removal of the
  proposed additional Conference and Training funding proposed for the City Attorney Cost
  Center (Item 2):

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, June 6, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 2 of 4

5.  New and Old Business (continued)

5A.  (continued)

  CONSENSUS ITEMS AND DIRECTED MODIFICATIONS
  No. Title
  1.  CCPA endowment fund revenue sources identification
  (Consensus #303)
  2.  Conference and training funding (eliminating $14,400 of proposed
  additional funding in the City Attorney Cost Center)
  (Consensus #304)
  3.  Potable water and sewer master plans
  (Consensus #305 and #306)
  4.  City Hall Security Improvements
  (Consensus #307 and #308)
  5.  Council Chambers Audio/Video Equipment Upgrades
  (Consensus #309)
  6.  Heritage Park Island and Lake Projects
  (Consensus #310 and #311)
  7.  Funding for an Employee and Classification and Compensation Study
  (City Council majority vote, May 12, 2022)
  8.  Inflation Considerations
  (City Council direction, May 16, 2022)
  9.  Clarification of City Commission Benefits Line Item
  (City Council direction, May 16, 2022)
  10. Rehabilitation of Arterial and Residential Streets
  (City Council majority vote, May 26, 2022)
  11. Cerritos Electric Utility Revenue and Operating Budget Update
  12. *This item was considered under a separate motion and is detailed
  in the next section of the minutes
  13. Rehabilitation/Replacement of Sewer Lift Stations CIP Update
  14. Additional CIP Projects for Consideration

  and;

  2. Present all City Council-directed items and modifications during the Fiscal Year 2022-23
  City Budget Adoption Public Hearing scheduled for the Thursday, June 23, 2022, 7:00
  p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Councilmember Johnson recused herself from the discussion, deliberation, and vote on the
  following item and was absent from the meeting until the item was concluded.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, June 6, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 3 of 4

5.  New and Old Business (continued)

5A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Include the financial adjustments and modifications recommended by staff for Item 12
  summarized below (Items are detailed in the associated agenda report for this item) to
  the proposed Fiscal Year 2022-23 budget resolution:

  CONSENSUS ITEMS AND DIRECTED MODIFICATIONS
  No. Title
  12. Sheriff’s Station Operational Improvements CIP Update

  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Johnson (recused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  At the conclusion of the vote on the above referenced item, Councilmember Johnson
  rejoined the meeting and was present through the meeting’s adjournment.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to appoint Mayor Pro Tem Barrows
  to serve as Chair of the City Council’s Budget/Finance Committee.

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  **For clarification purposes the total adjustments and modifications approved to be added
  to the proposed Fiscal Year 2022-23 Comprehensive Financial Plan as a result of Agenda
  Item 5A are as follows:

  FY 2022-23
  Operations  CIP

  TOTAL ADJUSTMENTS  $ 364,900  $ 11,942,000

5B.  Review and consideration of increasing the Cerritos Library’s hours of operation (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian and Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, June 6, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 4 of 4

5.  New and Old Business (continued)

5B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Increase the Cerritos Library's hours of operation by adding two hours on
  Saturday and Sunday, for a total of 52 hours of service per week. To
  accommodate the additional operating hours, increase the part-time earnings
  allocation by $135,280 for a total of $1,758,650 and increase the part-time
  employee benefits budget by $52,750, for a total of $685,790. Increase the
  Environmental Services Division budget within the Public Works Department
  budget by $9,500 to cover the increased custodial services hours (for a grand
  total budget increase of $197,530) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

5C.  Review and consideration of increasing the Cerritos Senior Center’s hours of operation
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Chelsea Askey, Community Participation Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, as amended, to direct the City
  Manager to:

  1. Provide staffing to accommodate designated club meetings to once per week; and

  2. Return to pre-pandemic hours of operation, including increasing operational hours to
  5:00 p.m. (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

6.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:19 p.m.

  /s/ Vida Barone  __________
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
